prompt:
Convert the contact block in the user message into JSON. Emit exactly one object and nothing else. Its required keys are "name", "phone", "email", "company", and "country"; every value is a JSON string or null.

Read the input as a note containing one contact block. Identify its labeled lines even if labels are abbreviated or reordered or the delimiter is a colon, equals sign or tab. Split at the label delimiter; do not split away punctuation inside values. Ignore everything outside the block. Trim and collapse whitespace in each value. Mark absent lines, blank values and the following whole-value tokens as missing, ignoring case: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.

Route the values before editing them. Reserve the country line for country. Route a value containing @ to email even under another label. To identify a phone under any label, strip initial tel: and a trailing extension (ext., ext, x, # or extension followed by digits); the remainder must contain at least seven digits and consist only of digits, spaces and + - ( ) . /. For name and company, follow the labels unless the name-line value has a trailing legal suffix and the company-line value does not: in that case take the name from the company line and the company from the name line. Match legal suffixes case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

Resolve phone and country with these branches:
- First map a supplied country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Recognize English, Swedish and German country names, two- and three-letter ISO codes and common aliases, regardless of case. UK and Great Britain map to GB, Holland to NL, USA and U.S.A. to US, Türkiye to TR, Czech Republic to CZ.
- If a supplied phone, without tel: or extension and ignoring a leading opening parenthesis, begins with + or 00, it is international. Remove literal (0) before deleting spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Replace opening 00 with +. Keep the number’s own calling code. If the country was missing, fill it from that code only when the code belongs to exactly one country. Shared codes such as +1 and +7 give null. A supplied country always wins for the country slot, not for the phone slot.
- Otherwise a supplied phone is national. If the record has no country, phone is null. If it does, strip formatting punctuation and spaces, remove one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the country calling code. Both branches produce E.164 strings (one plus followed only by digits).

Normalize the remaining slots:
- Name: if there is a comma, split at the first one and put the portion after it first. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof (case-insensitive, optional dot). For each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. Keep all Unicode letters and accents; never transliterate.
- Company: remove a trailing listed suffix and any comma directly before it. For each space-separated word, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest.
- Email: unwrap angle brackets and remove the mailto: prefix, including when one wrapper encloses the other. Lowercase the whole address without adding whitespace.

Trim the results and collapse internal whitespace runs. Check that every nonmissing assigned value was processed and that every key appears. Use null for missing values; the international-phone country fallback is the only exception. Never derive a value from surrounding text, a signature, a domain or a company suffix.
